title: Nut-Free Banana Cupcakes with Vanilla Swirl
shortDescription: Soft banana cupcakes with a vanilla swirl frosting, ready in about 43 minutes with 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake.
description: These cupcakes use very ripe, spotty bananas for real sweetness and a soft, moist crumb. I mash mine with a fork right in the mixing bowl, no blender needed. The batter stays light because we do not overload it with extra banana, just enough for flavor without density. A plain vanilla buttercream gets swirled with a touch more vanilla bean paste for a pretty marbled look on top. No nuts touch this kitchen when I make this batch, so it is safe for school bake sales and nut-free classrooms. I tested this recipe three times to get the crumb soft but sturdy enough to hold the frosting swirl. These are great for using up bananas that are too ripe to eat plain. The batter comes together in one bowl with a whisk, no mixer required for the cake part.
ingredients: 1 cup mashed ripe banana (about 2 large bananas)
1 cup unsalted butter, softened, for frosting
1 tsp vanilla bean paste (or vanilla extract)
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12 cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk flour, baking soda, salt, and cinnamon together in a medium bowl.
Beat 1/2 cup butter and granulated sugar until light and fluffy, about 2 minutes.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each one.
Mix in mashed banana, sour cream, and 1 tsp vanilla extract until combined.
Fold the flour mixture into the wet ingredients by hand, just until no dry streaks remain.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack.
For frosting, beat 1 cup butter until creamy, then add powdered sugar in two additions.
Split the frosting into two bowls. Stir vanilla bean paste into one half only.
Add both frostings side by side into a piping bag fitted with a large star tip, then pipe onto cooled cupcakes for a swirl effect.
tips: Use bananas with lots of brown spots. They mash easier and taste sweeter.
Do not overmix the batter once flour goes in, or the crumb turns tough.
Chill the piping bag 10 minutes if your kitchen is warm, so the swirl holds its shape.
Store cupcakes in the fridge if not eating within a day, since banana cake spoils faster than plain vanilla.

faq.question: Can I use frozen bananas for this recipe?
faq.answer: Yes, thaw them fully first and drain off extra liquid. Blot with a paper towel so the batter does not turn watery.

faq.question: Why is my banana cupcake dense instead of light?
faq.answer: This usually means too much banana or overmixed batter. Stick to 1 cup mashed banana and fold gently once flour is added.

faq.question: How do I get a clean two tone swirl on top?
faq.answer: Load both frostings into the same piping bag side by side, not stacked. Pipe in one steady motion without stopping.

faq.question: Is this recipe safe for a nut-free school bake sale?
faq.answer: Yes, every ingredient listed here is nut-free. Just check your specific brands of chocolate chips or sprinkles if you add extras.

conclusion: These banana cupcakes give you a soft, moist bite without feeling heavy. The vanilla swirl on top makes them look bakery made, but the whole batch mixes by hand. Keep them nut-free and simple for any bake sale or lunchbox treat.
